notes: DESIGN NOT TRUSTWORTHY FOR FLIGHT OR CONSTRUCTION: no airworthy operating point exists in the final sweep; reported operating point misses the static-margin window; static margin changes sign inside its evaluation window. The optimization result remains useful diagnostically, but its headline objective is not an airworthy design recommendation.

NO AIRWORTHY OPERATING POINT EXISTS IN THIS SWEEP. Every one of the 17 speeds that trimmed breaks at least one airworthiness rule, so there was nothing legal to choose from and what is reported is the least-bad ILLEGAL point: static margin 0.05719 against a 0.08 limit; minimum local static margin -0.01535 against a 0 limit. This is not a design. Read the objective as an upper bound the aeroplane cannot actually reach, and fix the aircraft — balance, control throw or wing loading — before reading anything else in this artifact.
Stall via wing-level CLmax knockdown; critical-section method arrives at M2/M3.
Smooth polars only; tripped-polar dual evaluation arrives at M2.
Propulsion chain is uncalibrated (no measurement path) — rankings over absolutes.

NOT PROVEN INFEASIBLE — trim did not converge at V = 8.0 m/s (the 2-D root-find ran out of progress from every start it was given). These points are excluded from the sweep because there is no operating point to report, not because none exists; read them as unknown rather than as a limit of the aeroplane.

STATIC MARGIN CHANGES SIGN INSIDE ITS OWN WINDOW: the reported 0.0572 is a least-squares slope over [-2.0, 0.0, 2.0] deg about trim, but the LOCAL dCm/dCL at alpha = 6.23 deg is -0.0153 — the aircraft is not positively stable there on this model. Cm(alpha) nonlinearity is the known dominant fidelity limit of this SM estimator (FINDINGS); treat the margin as an average, and do not fly the CG on the strength of it alone.

Static margin is OUT of range at the re-evaluation's reported speed (9.500 m/s), although the NLP met the window at 9.742 m/s (SM 0.08000). NO point in the sweep passed every airworthiness rule, so this is the least-bad ILLEGAL fallback, not an all-clear.

The static margin's sign change SURVIVES a 16-panel mesh (0.0572 → 0.0534), so refinement does not explain it. Combined with an inviscid VLM sweep that is monotone over the same window, the nonlinearity is the VISCOUS Cm at this Reynolds number — treat it as a property of the aeroplane.
CHAMPION STATIC MARGIN IS MESH-DEPENDENT: 0.0572 at the in-loop resolution against 0.0534 at 16 panels/section. The stability window is 0.07 wide and this moves the answer inside it.

STATIC-MARGIN SIGN FLIP IS NOT CONFIRMED BY AN INDEPENDENT METHOD: LiftingLine reports a local dCm/dCL going negative inside the window, but the VLM sweep over the same alphas is monotone and returns SM = 0.0530 against LL's 0.0572. The two methods differ by viscosity, so this does not settle which is right — it localizes the nonlinearity to LL's viscous Cm or its discretization, and the margin should not be treated as failing on LL's word alone.

THE FINENESS CEILING IS BINDING: the pod sits at f = 8.000000 against a declared ceiling of 8. That ceiling is a MODEL-validity bound — the Hoerner form factor keeps falling to f ~ 16 while the real minimum-drag band for a body of revolution is f ~ 6-7 — so the optimizer is being stopped by a declared number rather than by the aeroplane, and the slenderness it wants is not established to be real. Landing on it is a defect report against the fuselage drag model, not an optimum.

THE BOAT-TAIL FLOOR IS STILL ACTIVE: pod_tail sits at 1.800000 x d_eq against a floor of 1.8, with theta_max 18.9 deg against a 12 deg separation threshold. The floor is a PROXY for the afterbody physics and was kept for one battery to find out whether the new base-drag term had made it inactive. It has not: the term does not hold the tail cone open on its own, so the floor must NOT be deleted as a measured no-op and the correlation constants are what to revisit (docs/FUSELAGE_DRAG_PLAN.md 7).
